name: Gelkis Village
summary: In southwestern Desolace, the earth-aligned Gelkis centaur clan holds its village and guards the southern route. Their ravine overlooks the north-south road, making passage perilous for travelers without the clan’s favor.

sections.title: A Fortress in the Ravine
sections.body:
Gelkis Village fills a deep gorge between steep bluffs and rope bridges. The Gelkis have made their ancestral grounds a lasting fortress, with outposts reaching toward the Feralas border. Khan Shaka leads the warriors from Bolgan's Hole, a cavern in the southern cliff face.

Travelers heading south through Desolace must fight through the gorge or tread carefully. The Gelkis consider uninvited wanderers fair game in their endless war with rival centaur clans.

faq.answer: The Gelkis clan lives in the village, one of Desolace’s warring centaur tribes. They worship the earth and follow Khan Shaka, who resides in Bolgan's Hole, a cavern in the cliff.

faq.q: Why are the Gelkis centaur hostile to outsiders?
aliases: can i be friendly with gelkis
faq.answer: The Gelkis are territorial and hostile toward outsiders, and they hate the rival Magram clan above all. Hunting Magram warriors can earn their trust and safe passage into the village.

Gelkis Village lies in southwestern Desolace, just east and slightly south of Shadowprey Village, a troll settlement. Its ravines border the southern mountain face and overlook the trail leading south into Feralas.
Bolgan's Hole is a large cavern in the ravine’s southern rock wall, linked to the village by elevated bridges and bluffs. It is the Gelkis Khan’s inner sanctuary and seat of power.

angles.text: As a tauren, you know the centaurs have driven your people from their ancestral lands for generations. The Gelkis fortifications are a bitter reminder of their lasting threat to Kalimdor.

As a member of the Horde, you face the Gelkis’ fortified presence near Shadowprey Village, a Darkspear settlement on the coast directly to the west. The Gelkis remain a threat to nearby Horde operations.
